subject: Dedicated sizing: burst shaping & latency tolerances for FluxData
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fluxdata.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@fluxdata.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Mar 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake — initial telemetry and burst question

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As promised, attaching a small slice of our telemetry and a short description of how our product drives spikes. High level:
- Primary use case: interactive chat assistant embedded in our merchant dashboard.
- Normal steady-state: ~150 requests/minute across the region; each request is a short prompt (avg 45 tokens) with a model response ~140 tokens.
- Burst profile: when a merchant performs a bulk action or an A/B send, we see short bursts up to ~2,400 requests/min in a 20s window from a single tenant.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions per tenant 3–6, heavy tenants 60–120 during peak burst.

We need guidance on:
1) How we should think about dedicated pool sizing for worst-case per-tenant bursts vs shared fallback options.
2) Expected P50/P95/P99 latencies for a 2k-token-turnaround (prompt+response) on your recommended GPU SKU.

Attached: flux_telemetry_sample.csv (3k rows sample). Can you confirm what additional slices you need?

Appreciate it — happy to hop back on a quick call.

Sarah
Senior Product Manager
FluxData
[attachment: flux_telemetry_sample.csv (csv)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fluxdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Mar 2029 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — initial telemetry and burst question

Sarah — thanks for the sample and the clear burst description. Attached is a tiny dedicated-sizer template that will help us translate your telemetry into GPU footprint and SLOs. Key asks from our side (short checklist):

- Provide a 24h token histogram if possible (prompt and response tokens separated) — helps with sequence-length distribution.
- Mark which tenants are "heavy" and approximate number of concurrent sessions during the 20s burst.
- Tell us the acceptable P99 latency for the merchant-facing flow (is 500ms acceptable, or do you need <300ms?).
- Confirm whether degraded-mode (smaller model / lower temperature) is acceptable during rare overloads.

I've cc'd Marissa (pricing & commitments) and Karthik (inference sizing) so we can align on fallback options and a recommended GPU mix. I sketched two quick scenarios in the sheet: conservative (no fallbacks, headroom for 1.5x burst) and permissive (allow model fallbacks and 2x burst absorption with queueing).

Next steps: fill the template and send back; we can run a batch sizing pass and come back with a model/GPU mix + estimated committed capacity and cost delta. If you prefer, we can run a 30m sizing review tomorrow.

Attachments: dedicated_sizer_template.xlsx

—Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[attachment: dedicated_sizer_template.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fluxdata.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@fluxdata.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — initial telemetry and burst question

Jonas — thanks, attached we returned the completed template and a short tenant map. Highlights:
- Token histogram attached in the sheet (sheet tab: token_hist). Median prompt 42, median response 136, 98th percentile combined tokens ~620.
- We flagged 12 heavy tenants; during promotional sends they average 80 concurrent sessions each in the 20s burst.
- P99 requirement: merchant-facing primary flow wants <=450ms. Background analytics queries can be 2–3s.
- Degraded-mode: acceptable for non-critical tenants but not for top-3 heavy tenants. For those, we need deterministic latency.

We also included a simulated daily peak where 6 heavy tenants burst simultaneously (screenshot in sheet) — that's the scenario we want to avoid failing.

Attached: completed dedicated_sizer_template.xlsx, flux_telemetry_sample.csv (unchanged).

On the P99: can you call out recommended GPU SKUs and an expected P99 for each? We are comparing an aggressive commit vs smaller reserved pool + hosted overflow.

Thanks,
Sarah
[attachment: dedicated_sizer_template.xlsx (xlsx); attachment: flux_telemetry_sample.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fluxdata.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — initial telemetry and burst question

Sarah — this is very helpful, thanks for the level of detail. A few clarifying points before we run a formal sizing pass:

- When you say "deterministic latency" for your top-3 tenants, do you mean strict SLA-backed latency (we can include in Dedicated contract), or soft priority within a tenantized pool? We'll price both options: SLA-backed reserved lanes vs tenant-priority scheduling.
- For the 6-tenant simultaneous burst scenario: are all bursts aligned to the same second, or staggered across the 20s window? The latter materially reduces peak concurrency.
- Are you open to a hybrid fallback: reserved capacity sized for 2 of the top heavy tenants + a burst buffer on hosted capacity that would be used only when auto-provisioning is triggered? This often reduces committed costs while keeping deterministic behavior for the highest-value tenants.

Karthik — any immediate sizing notes from an inference perspective?

Jonas — once we have the full sheet clarified on alignment and whether SLA-backed lanes are required, we can produce:
1) recommended reserved GPU count (and SKUs) for the conservative scenario,
2) recommended reserved GPU + hosted overflow plan with cost delta,
3) suggested fallback model quantization/temperature policies per tenant class.

Sarah — happy to set up a short call to run through the outcomes tomorrow 10–10:30am PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

—Marissa
Head of Deal Ops, Redwood Inference
